OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The guard is deleted; whistle.py calls `CreatureCmd.stun(ctx.hooks, target)` unconditionally, as Whistle.cs:33 does. `CreatureCmd.Stun` has NO liveness test in either overload (CreatureCmd.cs:870-903) -- not even a CombatState null-check -- and the sim's `CreatureCmd.stun` (cmds.py) matches: a MachineMonster transition test and nothing else. Pinned by test_can_receive_powers.py::test_whistle_stuns_a_retained_corpse, where a removal-vetoed corpse ends the play with `stunned` True, which really does cost it the turn it would otherwise take (CombatManager.cs:1072-1090 iterates every creature still in the combat). This one needs no CanReceivePowers gate at all, which is why it is the member of the family whose fix is a pure deletion. Re-verified current on this stale-sweep pass: whistle.py:41 still calls `CreatureCmd.stun(ctx.hooks, target)` with no guard.  The text it replaced read: The damage is faithful and the STUN is the right verb. The divergence is the sim's extra `if not target.is_gone:` before it. C# calls `CreatureCmd.Stun(cardPlay.Target)` UNCONDITIONALLY (Whistle.cs:33), and `Stun` has NO liveness guard at all -- it is a bare `creature.StunInternal(Wrapper, nextMoveId)` plus a VFX wrapper (CreatureCmd.cs:870-903), with no `IsAlive`, `IsHittable` or `CombatState != null` test anywhere in either overload. So this is the card/bash family with a different verb: for an ordinary kill the two agree (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, and removal at 523-525 detaches the creature), but for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:159-161, moved from :100-104) the game STUNS it and the sim does not -- and a retained corpse still takes turns, so being stunned actually skips one. LIVE: the retained-corpse path is ported (ReattachPower, powers.py:2933-2938, moved from :2360-2365 -- content re-verified current, same withered/reattach shape; `combat.py:649,653,655` for `is_performing_move`/`combat_removal_committed`, moved from the historical :292,306 citation) and Whistle is a ported Ancient from Tanx's Whistle. Same family and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3), and the only member of it whose payload is a STUN rather than a power -- so the observable is the corpse's skipped turn rather than a Vicious draw. Presentation, folded in: WithHitFx and the StunIntent hover tip (16).
